text:
No, almost certainly not. With 6 people, microservices trade a problem you probably don't have (independent team scaling, divergent deploy cadences) for ones you definitely will: distributed debugging, network failure modes, data consistency across services, versioned contracts, and more infra/ops work. That overhead would consume a large share of a 6-person team's capacity.

The strongest case for moving would be a concrete bottleneck, such as one component needing very different scaling or runtime characteristics (e.g., heavy ML inference or video processing), a hard compliance isolation requirement, or deploy contention between teams. None of those is implied by team size alone.

If the pain is real but unnamed (slow tests, tangled code, risky deploys), fix it inside the monolith first: enforce module boundaries (Packwerk, engines), speed up CI, and add feature flags. If a single component later does need to be pulled out, extract just that one.

If you tell me the specific pain driving the question, I can say whether it points to services or to something cheaper.
